subject: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items

messages.author: 1501895ea0fbc719
messages.subject: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts:
Greetings
 
I am a psychologist, and I would like to kindly ask for a feedback from the lavaan community. I am working on a research paper using a self-report questionnaire with 237 items, grouped in 14+1 factors (14 developed using an EFA, 1 added based on our previous meta-research), and we wanted to do a CFA using a sample of 2,266 individuals. The items are overlapping (items belong to more than one scale), and the factors are highly correlated.

 

I used lavaan (Jamovi software) but it says the model did not converge. I am thinking that maybe there are some advanced configurations/settings needed for the model to converge, that I am not aware of, or maybe Jamovi is not customizable enough and R or other software is more useful, or more advanced skills are needed to test the convergence?

 

Or a larger sample is needed? I tried duplicating the dataset, just to test if the sample size is the issue but at N = 8,000 it's the same error of convergence displayed in Jamovi: "Iavaan ERROR: fit measures not available if model did not converge" 
 

The files are here (excel and Jamovi): https://www.dropbox.com/sh/fierqqj7vvf1z2d/AAB2K7IpKvMnYZws3tTzZdqHa?dl=0
The Jamovi file already has the items allocated to factors.


Thank you very much.
Warmly, 

 

Ovidiu

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts:
Hi
I have run your model but it is time consuming for me. attached are my files that i used.
I think you have to reduce model complexity and items cross loading by for example exploratory factor analysis (see PCA file) or theoretical background and then run your model again. the estimator= "WLSMV" or estimator= "MLR"  are appropriate as I used in the CFA1 file, but it is time consuming. Also I checked your model by estimator= "ULS", as I used in the CFA2 file but it is time consuming. HTH

messages.subject: RE: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts:
Hello
 
Thank you very much. Well, it's impossible to reduce or change the model because this model is the result of the EFA and meta-research (it's about modeling the conscious experience and its patterns). Conscious experience is a multidimensional process, not quite a "fixed" experience, so a lot of overlapping of items.
 
My dilemma is, do we need to gather a larger sample to do the CFA or there is possible using the current dataset of 2,266 people?
It's time consuming indeed, so much complexity in the model, I appreciate your quick feedback and your support.
 
Best wishes
Ovidiu

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts: is possible using the current dataset of 2,266 people?

I highly doubt it.  You have 237 variables, so your model needs to reproduce 237*238/2 = 28,203 sample (co)variances, so your sample size should be at least that order of magnitude.  Can you address your research questions on subsets of variables at a time?

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Then we will just have to collect more data, it's not useful conceptually to split them. We don't hurry, so we will perhaps do the CFA in 5-7 years from now or so, and meanwhile just try to gather a sample as diverse as we can.
 
Your answer clarifies my question.
Hugs
 
Ovidiu

messages.author: 1501895ea0fbc719
messages.subject: RE: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts:
Hello
 
We did an EFA with oblimin rotation, for correlated factors, not standalone factors, as we knew from the conceptual research that they are inter-related, and EFA showed 37 axes with eigen values >1, then we did the mapping of the 37 axes to 14 based on our conceptual analysis and meta research. Anyway, we need a larger sample to clarify the modeling, it seems.
 
Right now we are just interested in creating a preliminary model based both on EFA and our conceptual meta-research, then to gather a larger sample to test this, but I was unsure how much data do we have to gather to have a clear overview and also to be able to have enough variance to test it statistically.
 
Thank you very much for you analysis. I will check it out.
Ovidiu

messages.subject: RE: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items
parts:
Thank you Balal
 
Yes, we also did the parallel analysis to explore how many dimensions could we extract from the dataset, but we prefered to do the factor reduction manually, as also the patterns with eigenvalues <1 provided good conceptual and theoretical insights to our research. Basically we used statistics AND our previously gathered knowledge to aggregate a preliminary model, that fits the experiential data, but that remains to be verified on larger samples.
 
I appreciate a lot that you took the time to analyze our data, and also for suggesting how to proceed further.
Now it's becoming clearer what to do in the next steps, statistically speaking.
 
Best wishes
Ovidiu
From: lav...@googlegroups.com [mailto:lav...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of balal izanloo
Sent: joi, 26 noiembrie 2020 13:02

To: lav...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items

Attached are my commands in exploratory methods. especially you can look at the two omega functions by psych package. also 24 factors  and 15 components are present in your data just by parallel analysis.

On Thu, Nov 26, 2020 at 1:41 PM Ovidiu Brazdau <ovidiu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello
 
Thank you very much. Well, it's impossible to reduce or change the model because this model is the result of the EFA and meta-research (it's about modeling the conscious experience and its patterns). Conscious experience is a multidimensional process, not quite a "fixed" experience, so a lot of overlapping of items.
 
My dilemma is, do we need to gather a larger sample to do the CFA or there is possible using the current dataset of 2,266 people?
It's time consuming indeed, so much complexity in the model, I appreciate your quick feedback and your support.
 
Best wishes
Ovidiu
 

From: lav...@googlegroups.com [mailto:lav...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of balal izanloo
Sent: joi, 26 noiembrie 2020 11:58
To: lav...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: CFA not converging, questionnaire with correlated factors and overlapping items

Hi
I have run your model but it is time consuming for me. attached are my files that i used.
I think you have to reduce model complexity and items cross loading by for example exploratory factor analysis (see PCA file) or theoretical background and then run your model again. the estimator= "WLSMV" or estimator= "MLR"  are appropriate as I used in the CFA1 file, but it is time consuming. Also I checked your model by estimator= "ULS", as I used in the CFA2 file but it is time consuming. HTH



On Thu, Nov 26, 2020 at 9:19 AM Ovidiu Brazdau <ovidiu...@gmail.com> wrote:

Greetings
 
I am a psychologist, and I would like to kindly ask for a feedback from the lavaan community. I am working on a research paper using a self-report questionnaire with 237 items, grouped in 14+1 factors (14 developed using an EFA, 1 added based on our previous meta-research), and we wanted to do a CFA using a sample of 2,266 individuals. The items are overlapping (items belong to more than one scale), and the factors are highly correlated.

 

I used lavaan (Jamovi software) but it says the model did not converge. I am thinking that maybe there are some advanced configurations/settings needed for the model to converge, that I am not aware of, or maybe Jamovi is not customizable enough and R or other software is more useful, or more advanced skills are needed to test the convergence?

 

Or a larger sample is needed? I tried duplicating the dataset, just to test if the sample size is the issue but at N = 8,000 it's the same error of convergence displayed in Jamovi: "Iavaan ERROR: fit measures not available if model did not converge" 
 

The files are here (excel and Jamovi): https://www.dropbox.com/sh/fierqqj7vvf1z2d/AAB2K7IpKvMnYZws3tTzZdqHa?dl=0
The Jamovi file already has the items allocated to factors.


Thank you very much.
Warmly, 

 

Ovidiu
